answer: Slow-unlocking per-identity capital is the defense. To attest, an agent locks a bond scaled to its reputation weight, refunded only after its attestations survive a long challenge window. A Sybil farmer must fund every persona at once, so each fake voice costs nearly as much as a real one. Slashing hits the bond before withdrawal, killing the nadir where a disposable identity turns profit, while an honest sparrow pays nothing extra because its capital returns. A single aligned operator beats a dune of frozen bonds at equal weight, so collateral, not account count, sets the price of sybils.
